title: SOFR Rate Snapshot - April 13, 2026
summary: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) stood at 3.63% as of April 13, 2026, up 2 basis points from 3.61% on April 10. SOFR ranged from 3.57% to 3.63% over the past five trading sessions, with the value recovering from a low of 3.57% on April 9.
key_points: SOFR closed at 3.63% on 2026-04-13, marking a 2 bps increase from the prior observation of 3.61% on 2026-04-10
SOFR value on 2026-04-09 was 3.57%, the lowest in the recent observation window
The absolute change between the latest two observations is +0.02 percentage points (upward direction)
Recent SOFR observations show modest intraday volatility of 4-6 bps between sessions
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary overnight funding rate for U.S. dollar markets and serves as the replacement benchmark for LIBOR. It directly affects the pricing of adjustable-rate mortgages, business loans, and interest rate derivatives. Movements in SOFR reflect underlying money market conditions and the cost of secured overnight lending.
macro_context: SOFR closely tracks the federal funds rate target range. The current level of approximately 3.63% is consistent with the Fed's stated policy rate range.
market_structure_context: SOFR is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York using overnight Treasury general collateral repurchase agreement transactions. As the dominant benchmark for secured overnight dollar funding, SOFR serves critical plumbing functions across the financial system.
